dervis-irab:56-63.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضُحًى): al-ḍuḥā is the sun shining forth after it has risen. The Arabs gave names to the hours of the day: the first is al-dhurūr, then al-buzūgh, then al-ḍuḥā, then al-ghazāla, then al-hājira, then al-zawāl, then al-dulūk, then al-ʿaṣr, then al-aṣīl, then al-ṣabūb, then al-ḥadūr, then al-ghurūb.
It is also said of them: al-bukūr, then al-shurūq, then al-ishrāq, then al-raʾd, then al-ḍuḥā, then al-mutūʿ, then al-zawāl, then al-hājira, then al-aṣīl, then al-ʿaṣr, then al-ṭafal, then al-ghurūb.
(فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ): He would destroy you; from the four-letter form أسحت, which is the dialect of Najd and Tamīm, meaning "to destroy". One also says سحت, which is the dialect of the Hijaz. The root of this material denotes exhausting something completely and bringing it to an end; from it comes «سحت الحالق الشعر», i.e. the shaver took the hair off completely and left none of it. It is used for destroying and doing away with something. In al-Qāmūs: «سحت يسحت, of the pattern fataḥa, and سحّت with doubling: he acquired suḥt, i.e. unlawful wealth; سحته: he destroyed him, uprooted him and slaughtered him; سحت الشحم عن اللحم: he peeled the fat off the meat; سحت وجه الأرض: he effaced it; أسحت: he corrupted it, destroyed it and uprooted it».

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْناهُ آياتِنا كُلَّها فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبى): The lām is the response to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); أريناه is a past verb from رأى in the sense of seeing with the eyes, but it takes two objects because the hamza of transfer has entered it; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); آياتنا is the second mafʿūl bihi; كلها is tawkīd (emphasis) of آياتنا; فكذب وأبى are conjoined to أريناه. The nine signs of Moses have already been mentioned, then the last two signs, namely the staff and the drawing out of the hand.
(قالَ أَجِئْتَنا لِتُخْرِجَنا مِنْ أَرْضِنا بِسِحْرِكَ يا مُوسى): قال is a past verb and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", i.e. Pharaoh; the clause أجئتنا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; جئتنا is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; لتخرجنا: the lām is for giving the reason, and تخرج is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of reason; نا is the mafʿūl bihi; من أرضنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تخرجنا, and بسحرك is attached to تخرجنا.
(فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلا أَنْتَ مَكاناً سُوىً): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and the lām is the response to an omitted oath, its implied form being "By Allah, we shall surely bring you"; بسحر is attached to نأتينك; مثله is a naʿt (adjective) of سحر. It is also permissible for بسحر to be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by magic like it in strangeness, which would oppose it and refute it". فاجعل: the fāʾ is a conjunction and اجعل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is "you"; بيننا is an adverb attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, and بينك is conjoined; موعدا is a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with a prefixed mīm), the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause لا نخلفه is a naʿt of موعدا; نحن is tawkīd of the pronoun in نخلفه; the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and أنت is conjoined to the pronoun in نخلفه. مكانا is a badal (substitute) from موعدا by implying a muḍāf, i.e. "the place of an appointment"; or مكانا may be parsed as accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in a place"; or you may make it accusative by the maṣdar, which is موعد. سوى is a naʿt, i.e. "midway", and it is read with ḍamma on the wāw and with kasra. This is one of several parsings which will come in the section on Benefits.
(قالَ: مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى): موعدكم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and يوم الزينة is the khabar (predicate); أن and what follows it are conjoined to يوم الزينة: either to اليوم, in which case the position of the maṣdar is nominative, or to الزينة, in which case its position is genitive. الناس is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and ضحى is an adverb attached to يحشر. The discussion of the Day of Adornment and the reason for choosing it will come.
(فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتى): The fāʾ is a conjunction; تولى is a past verb and فرعون is the fāʿil; فجمع is conjoined to فتولى; كيده is the mafʿūl bihi on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the possessors of his scheme", namely the sorcerers; ثم is a conjunction and أتى is conjoined to جمع. He expressed it with ثم to indicate that he spent time in gathering the sorcerers and drawing up plans.
(قالَ لَهُمْ مُوسى وَيْلَكُمْ لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً): قال is a past verb, لهم is attached to it, and موسى is the fāʿil; ويلكم is a maṣdar of imprecation whose verb the Arabs let die out, so it is accusative by an omitted verb; لا is prohibitive and تفتروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; على الله is attached to تفتروا, and كذبا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذابٍ وَقَدْ خابَ مَنِ افْتَرى): The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); يسحتكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation preceded by a prohibition; بعذاب is attached to يسحتكم. وقد: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and قد is a particle of affirmation; خاب is a past verb; من is the fāʿil, and the clause افترى is its ṣila (relative clause).
(فَتَنازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوى): The fāʾ is a conjunction; تنازعوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أمرهم is the mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition; بينهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; أسروا is conjoined to تنازعوا, and النجوى is the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. they concealed it, meaning they consulted one another in secret.
(قالُوا: إِنْ هذانِ لَساحِرانِ يُرِيدانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِما وَيَذْهَبا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلى): إن is lightened from the heavy (inna) and is inoperative; هذان is a demonstrative for the dual in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is the lām of distinction (al-lām al-fāriqa); ساحران is the khabar of هذان; the clause يريدان is a naʿt of ساحران; أن and what is within its scope are the object of يريدان; من أرضكم is attached to يخرجاكم; بسحرهما is a ḥāl, i.e. "accompanied by their magic"; يذهبا is conjoined to يخرجاكم; بطريقتكم is attached to يذهبا, and المثلى is a naʿt of طريقتكم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذابٍ وَقَدْ خابَ مَنِ افْتَرى» there is the device of radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā al-ṣadr (returning the end upon the beginning), which the later scholars called al-taṣdīr; it is lighter on the ear and more fitting to the context. Its discussion has already been given, and we add here that Ibn al-Muʿtazz divided it into three types:
The first is where the last word of the first hemistich agrees with the last word of the second hemistich, or is homogeneous with it, as in the saying of one of them:
يلقى إذا ما كان يوم عرمرم ... في جيش رأي لا يفل عرمرم
(He meets, when there is a day of a vast army, [the foe] in an army of counsel that is not blunted — vast.)
The second type is where the last word of the verse agrees with its first word, as in the saying of another:
سريع إلى ابن العم يلطم وجهه ... وليس إلى داعي الندى بسريع
(Quick to his cousin, to slap his face, but not quick to the one who calls to generosity.)
The third type is where the last word of the verse agrees with part of a word in its first hemistich, as in his saying:
سقى الرمل صوب مستهل غمامه ... وما ذاك إلا حب من حل بالرمل
(May the downpour of its pouring cloud water al-Raml — and that is only out of love for the one who dwells at al-Raml.)
Shaykh Zakī al-Dīn ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ said: «What would be good is that the first type be called taṣdīr al-taqfiya (rhyme-taṣdīr), the second taṣdīr al-ṭarafayn (taṣdīr of the two ends), and the third taṣdīr al-ḥashw (taṣdīr of the middle)». The examples of this are many.

* Benefits:
The parsers differed greatly over the saying of the Exalted «فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلا أَنْتَ مَكاناً سُوىً», and the truth is that it is one of the most difficult constructions. In the I'rab we chose the best of the options, the closest to logic and the nearest to ease. There remain matters that must be clarified:
موعدا: there is disagreement about it, along the following lines:
a- It is a noun of time; this is favoured by His saying «قالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ», and the meaning is "appoint for us a time of meeting"; that is why he answered them with his saying: «موعدكم يوم الزينة».
b- It is a noun of place; this is favoured by His saying «مَكاناً سُوىً», and the meaning is "make clear to us a known place which we and you know, so that you come to it".
c- It is a mīmī maṣdar meaning "promise", and an omitted muḍāf is implied, i.e. "the place of a promise". This is supported by His saying «لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت», because an appointment is described as being broken or not broken. This is what we chose.
If you make it a time, two things are binding on you: that you make the time something broken, and that what governs مكانا in the accusative is left over for you [Translator's note: i.e. you are left without a governor for مكانا]. If you make it a place, it is also binding on you to make the breaking fall on the place, and His saying «موعدكم يوم الزينة» would not correspond. So what remains is to make it a maṣdar meaning "promise", to imply an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the place of an appointment", to make the pronoun in نخلفه refer to the appointment, and to make مكانا a badal from the omitted مكان.
Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed مكانا to be accusative as the second object of جعل [Translator's note: the source prints «لا جعل قالا», apparently a corruption of «لاجعل، قالا» "of اجعل; they said"]; they said: موعدا on this view is also a place, and مكانا is not made accusative by موعدا because it is a maṣdar which has been qualified — meaning that it is valid as a second object, but on the condition that الموعد means the place, so as to correspond to the khabar.
Al-Ḥūfī made مكانا accusative as an adverb, made accusative by اجعل. Thus there result five options for the accusative of مكانا:
1- That it is a badal from the omitted مكانا.
2- That it is the second object of جعل.
3- That it is accusative by an implied verb.
4- That it is accusative by the maṣdar itself.
5- That it is accusative as an adverb by اجعل itself.
We cited these opinions only because they are close, and because taking them all in is extremely useful; so reflect.

dervis-irab:64-70.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَأَجْمِعُوا): i.e. resolve upon your scheme and make it something agreed upon, so that you do not differ, like a question on which there is consensus. One says: اجمعوا الأمر and اجمعوا عليه. «فلانة بجمع» means she is a virgin; «ضربه بجمع كفه» (he struck him with his fist); «استجمع لفلان أمره» (his affair came together for him); «استجمع السيل» (the torrent gathered); and «استجمع الفرس جريا» (the horse gathered itself in running). He said, describing a mirage:
ومستجمع جريا وليس ببارح ... تباريه في ضاحي المتان سواعده
(One gathering itself to run yet not leaving its place, its streams vying with it on the sun-exposed hard ground.)
i.e. its channels. «استجمع الوادي» is said when no spot of the valley remains without flowing. It is reported from one of the Arabs: «Al-Rumma and Falj do not flow in full; they only flow in their sides and their outskirts». «استجمع القوم»: the people all went. «جمعوا لبني فلان»: they massed to fight them: «إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ». «أجمعت القدر غليا»: the pot came to a full boil. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ونحشّ تحت القدر نوقدها ... بغضا الغريف فأجمعت تغلي
(And we stoke beneath the pot, kindling it with the ghaḍā wood of the thicket, until it came fully to the boil.)
And among the metonymies: «فلانة قد جمعت الثياب», i.e. she has grown up, because she wears the shift, the head-covering and the wrap.
(فَأَوْجَسَ): al-ījās is concealing; ījās al-khawf is concealing something of fear. Likewise «توجس الصوت» is to hear a slight sound of it. That was due to the nature of the human constitution.
(تَلْقَفْ): it swallows; its root meaning is taking something quickly. He said in al-Qāmūs: «لقف يلقف, of the pattern taʿiba, laqfan; and التقف الشيء: he took it quickly».

* I'rab:
(فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلى): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. if the matter is as has been mentioned — that the two of them are sorcerers, etc. — then resolve upon your scheme and make it agreed upon, such that not one of you holds back from it. أجمعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كيدكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if you regard أجمعوا as transitive; some did not regard it as transitive, in which case كيدكم is accusative by removal of the preposition. ثم ائتوا is conjoined to أجمعوا, and صفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). He only ordered them to do so in order to put fear into the breasts of the onlookers. Abū ʿUbayda said: al-ṣaff is the place of assembly, and the place of prayer is called al-ṣaff. Al-Zajjāj said: on this view its meaning is "then come to the place in which you gather for your festival and your prayer"; one says «أتيت الصف» meaning "I came to the place of prayer". On this view it is accusative as an object.
وقد: the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) and قد is a particle of affirmation; أفلح is a past verb; اليوم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) أفلح; من is the fāʿil of أفلح, and the clause استعلى is the ṣila (relative clause).
(قالُوا يا مُوسى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقى): إما is a particle of condition and detailing; its meaning here is giving a choice, and it only occurs after a request. أن and what follows it are in the sense of a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "choose one of the two matters"; or nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is your throwing"; or a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, the implied form being "your throwing is first". وإما أن نكون is conjoined to what preceded; the ism of نكون is implied, its implied form being "we"; أول is its khabar; من is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause ألقى is the ṣila. It is also permissible for أن and what is within its scope to be in the position of accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "choose your throwing first, or our throwing".
(قالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا فَإِذا حِبالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّها تَسْعى): بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; ألقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. فإذا: the fāʾ is conjoining to something omitted, its implied form being "so they threw, and behold"; this إذا is for surprise (al-mufājaʾa). It has already been stated that it is a particle or an adverb, and then there is disagreement whether it is an adverb of place or of time. We shall quote the saying of al-Zamakhsharī, for it is the utmost of the utmost. He said:
«The precise account of it is that it is the إذا which denotes time, which requires something to govern it in the accusative and a clause to which it is annexed; in some places it has been restricted to having as its governor a specific verb, namely the verb of surprise, while the clause is nominal and nothing else. So the implied form of the saying of the Exalted «فَإِذا حِبالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ» is: "Moses came suddenly upon the time of the illusion of the moving of their ropes and staffs". This is a representation, and the meaning is his coming suddenly upon their ropes and staffs made to seem to him to be moving».
حبالهم is a mubtadaʾ, عصيهم is conjoined to it, and the clause يخيل إليه is the khabar of حبالهم. If you make إذا the khabar, then the clause يخيل إليه is a ḥāl. من سحرهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخيل. أنها: أنّ and its ism, and the clause تسعى is the khabar of أنّ; أنّ and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يخيل, i.e. "their moving is made to seem to him". Al-Zamakhsharī made the maṣdar a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from the pronoun in حبالهم and عصيهم.
(فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسى): The fāʾ is a conjunction and أوجس is a past verb; في نفسه is attached to أوجس; خيفة is the mafʿūl bihi and موسى is the fāʿil.
(قُلْنا لا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلى): قلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause لا تخف is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); لا is prohibitive and تخف is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you". The clause إنك is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), as a giving of the reason for the prohibition of the fear which assailed him owing to the human nature of faintness of heart, even though he was certain that Allah was his helper and that they would not reach him with harm. إنّ and its ism; أنت is tawkīd (emphasis), or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ; الأعلى is the khabar of إنّ, or the khabar of أنت, with the clause then being the khabar of إنّ. Discussion of the intensification in this expression will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَأَلْقِ ما فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا): وألق: the wāw is a conjunction and ألق is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; ما is the mafʿūl bihi; في يمينك is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما. The secret of this vagueness will come in the section on Rhetoric. تلقف is the response to the command, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn; the fāʿil of تلقف is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it (fem.)"; ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause صنعوا is the ṣila, i.e. what they had falsified and lied about.
(إِنَّما صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ ساحِرٍ وَلا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتى): The giving of the reason for His saying تلقف. إنّ and its ism [Translator's note: i.e. ما, a relative noun as the ism of إنّ]; the clause صنعوا is the ṣila, and كيد ساحر is the khabar of إنّ. The Muṣḥaf has followed the practice of writing ما joined to إنّ. It is also permissible for ما to be maṣdariyya, and the parsing is the same. ولا: the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction and لا is negative; يفلح الساحر is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; حيث is an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, attached to يفلح, and the clause أتى is annexed to the adverb.
(فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّداً قالُوا: آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هارُونَ وَمُوسى): The fāʾ conjoins to an omitted clause, its implied form being "so Moses threw his staff, and it swallowed all that they had made". فألقي is a passive past verb; السحرة is the nāʾib fāʿil; سجدا is a ḥāl of السحرة. قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause آمنا is the object of the saying, and it is a verb and its fāʿil; برب هارون وموسى is attached to آمنا.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are devices of eloquence (bayān) which astonish the mind. The first of them:

1- The device of al-istidrāj (drawing on the opponent)
Discussion of it has already been given. In addition to the eloquence in it, it contains subtle points in drawing on the opponent and forcing him to submit and concede. At the start the sorcerers wished to draw Moses on, confident that they would prevail over him; and it was as if Allah inspired them with good manners towards Moses in giving him the choice and granting him fairness from themselves when they said «فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً لا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلا أَنْتَ مَكاناً سُوىً», so they left the setting of the appointment to him. But Moses, by inspiration from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, drew them on to make their appointment the day of their adornment and their festival, so that the truth would be clear before the eyes of the witnesses, and so be more disgracing to their scheme and more tearing of their cover. And when they drew him on to the choice of throwing — whether he would be the one to begin or they would be the ones to begin — he drew them on to make them begin with what they had, so that his throwing of the staff afterwards would be a hurling of the truth against falsehood, so that it smashes it, and behold, it vanishes. How splendid is this speech!

2- The device of emphasising with the two pronouns
You may ask: what is the relation of a grammatical discussion to rhetoric? Pronouns and the emphasising of some of them by others are mentioned in the books of grammar. We say that the matter is more sublime and more elevated than grammar, and the grammarians are remote from this lofty art. By emphasising with the two pronouns we mean that the attached pronoun is emphasised by the detached one, as in your saying «إنك أنت»; or the detached one is emphasised by a detached one like it, as in your saying «أنت أنت»; or the attached one is emphasised by an attached one like it, as in your saying «إنك إنك لعالم». This sort of thing is only brought in the context of intensification, and it is one of the secrets of the science of bayān. Of this is the saying of the Exalted «قالُوا يا مُوسى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ» [Translator's note: this wording is from al-Aʿrāf 7:115, not the verse of Ṭāhā under discussion, which reads «أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقى»]. The sorcerers' wish to throw before Moses was not known to him, because they did not state openly what was in their minds about that; but when they turned away from matching their address to Moses with its like, to emphasising what pertained to them with the two pronouns, namely نكون and نحن, that indicated that they wished to precede him and to throw before him. For matching their address to Moses with its like would have required that they say: "Either you throw or we throw", so that the two clauses would be parallel. Since they said of themselves «وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ نَحْنُ الْمُلْقِينَ», this saying was taken as evidence of their desire to throw before him. Also of this is the saying of the Exalted «فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسى قُلْنا لا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلى». The emphasising with the two pronouns here, in His saying «إنك أنت الأعلى», is more effective in removing fear from the heart of Moses and more establishing of victory and mastery. Had He said: "Do not fear, you are the uppermost" [Translator's note: the source prints «إنك الأعلى أنت الأعلى»], it would not have had the confirmation and establishment of the removal of fear that His saying «إنك أنت الأعلى» has. In these three words there are six benefits:
1- The doubled «إنّ», whose function is to affirm what comes after it and to emphasise it. The scholars of maʿānī have stated that the report with إنّ is either ṭalabī (addressed to one seeking) or inkārī (addressed to one denying), not ibtidāʾī (addressed to one with no prior notion), as when you say «زيد قائم» and then say «إن زيدا قائم»: in your saying «إن زيدا قائم» there is an affirmation of Zayd's standing that is not in your saying «زيد قائم».
2- The repetition of the pronoun in His saying «إنك أنت». Had He confined Himself to one of the two pronouns, it would not have had this standing in confirming the victory of Moses and affirming his mastery.
3- The lām of definition in His saying «الأعلى»; He did not say «أعلى» or «عال», because had He said that, He would have made it indefinite and it would have been suitable for every single one of its kind, as in your saying «رجل», which is suitable to apply to every single man; whereas if you say «الرجل», you have singled him out from among men by definiteness and made him well known among them. Likewise His saying «إنك أنت الأعلى» came, i.e. to the exclusion of others.
4- The form afʿal, whose function is preference (tafḍīl); He did not say «العالي»; so he is higher than every high one.
5- The word of height (ʿuluww), indicating that the victory is established for him from the aspect of height. It is known that the aim of His saying «الأعلى» is victory, except that in «الأعلى» there is an addition, namely its proceeding from a high place.
6- The resumption (istiʾnāf), namely the saying of the Exalted «لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى»; He did not say «لأنك أنت الأعلى». That was more effective in making Moses, upon him be peace, certain of victory and ascendancy, and established it in the depth of his soul in a way that leaves no room at all for doubt.
A kind of this device has already been given, and others will come in their time and places, if Allah wills. It remains for you to speak about Moses' choice of the Day of Adornment; so what is this day?

The Day of Adornment:
It is said to be the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, or the Day of Nawrūz, or a festival day they had every year, on which they set up a market, adorned themselves and displayed all their finery, since people would be assembled on it from the forenoon until the evening.

3- The device of al-ibhām (vagueness):
This is in His saying «ما في يمينك». He made it vague for two opposite purposes. The first of them is belittling its matter, i.e. "Do not mind the multitude of their ropes and staffs, and throw the single little stick of small bulk which is in your hand, for by the power of Allah the Exalted it will swallow them, despite its being one and their being many, and its smallness and their greatness". The second is magnifying its matter, i.e. "Do not be concerned with these large and numerous bodies, for in your right hand there is something greater than all of them; so throw it, and it will efface them and do away with them, by the permission of Allah". Someone might say: how is the staff belittled?
The answer is that what is intended by belittling it beside the divine power is belittling the scheme of the sorcerers a fortiori; because if it — being the paltry, slight thing of no account in relation to the divine power — did away with the gilded deceptions and invented lies they had brought, then what do you think of their scheme, which the slightest thing can do away with? This is a subtle meaning which few perceive. The poet of immortality, Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, aspired to its heights, and said in an ode in which he praises Badr ibn ʿAmmār and mentions the lion which had rushed upon him, and he struck it with his whip:
أمعفر الليث الهزبر بسوطه ... لمن ادّخرت الصارم المصقولا؟
(O you who rolled the mighty lion in the dust with his whip — for whom have you saved the polished sword?)
The meaning is: if you meet this lion, the strongest and bravest of animals, with your whip, then for whom have you hidden your polished sword?
The masters of rhetoric also have a way of exalting praise by magnifying the army of the enemy of the one praised, so that from it there follows the magnifying of the army of the one praised, which overpowered it and took possession of it. Abū al-Ṭayyib aspired to its heights when he described the army of the Byzantines which Sayf al-Dawla met; he went to great lengths in magnifying its matter and depicting its great numbers, the aim being to go to the utmost in magnifying the matter of Sayf al-Dawla and his army. He said, describing the army of the Byzantines:
أتوك يجرون الحديد كأنهم ... سروا بجياد ما لهن قوائم
(They came to you dragging iron, as if they travelled by night on steeds that had no legs.)
إذا برقوا لم تعرف البيض منهم ... ثيابهم من مثلها والعمائم
(When they flashed, the swords could not be told apart from them; their garments and their turbans were of the same [steel].)
He made the Byzantines flash because of the great amount of iron on them, and did not distinguish between their swords and them, because on their heads were helmets and mail coifs and their garments were coats of mail, so they were like swords. By this description he pointed to the abundance of this army's weapons, as a preparation for pointing to its strength:
خميس بشرق الأرض والغرب زحفه ... وفي أذن الجوزاء منه زمازم
(An army in five divisions, its advance spanning the east of the earth and the west, and in the ear of Gemini there is a rumbling from it.)
تجمع فيه كل لسن وأمة ... فما تفهم الحداث إلا التراجم
(In it every tongue and nation gathered, so that none understood the speakers but interpreters.)
فلله وقت ذوب الغشّ ناره ... فلم يبق إلا صارم أو ضبارم
(What a time it was, whose fire melted away the dross, so that nothing remained but a sharp sword or a stout lion-hearted warrior!)
The completion of this marvellous description will come in another of the places of rhetoric in which Abū al-Ṭayyib aspired to the heights of the Quran.

Another subtle point in the vagueness:
There is another subtle point besides the intention of magnifying and belittling, namely that Moses, upon him be peace, first learned that the staff was a sign from Allah the Exalted when He asked him: «وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى», and then the Exalted showed him its sign. So when the time came when the sign needed to appear from it, the Exalted said: «وألق ما في يمينك», so that by this wording he would be awakened to the time when Allah the Exalted said to him «وَما تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ» and showed him its sign. That would be an alerting and a reassurance for him, since he was addressed with what he was accustomed to being addressed with at the time its sign appeared. That is a station suited to reassurance and steadying, in a situation in which the composure of even the strongest and firmest of souls departs.

4- The device of al-takrīr (repetition):
Its discussion and reference to it, and the mention of splendid examples of it, have frequently been given, and more and most will come. Here in these verses the word of throwing (ilqāʾ) is repeated, but it is a repetition that does not run on one pattern; rather it is one word in two opposite, contradictory meanings, by which He, Glorified is He, moved His servants from the utmost of disbelief and obstinacy to the end of faith and right guidance. How great is the difference between the two throwings: they threw their ropes and staffs for disbelief and denial; then, an hour later, they threw down their heads for gratitude and prostration.

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعُلى): it may be written with yāʾ or with alif, because the verb is علا يعلو and علي يعلى; it means rank and elevation. al-Suyūṭī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it is the plural of عليا, like كبرى and كبر, and so it was written with yāʾ.
(اسْتَوى): it has many meanings in the language. He said in al-Qāmūs: "استوى الشيء: it became even and straight; one says سويت الشيء فاستوى (I levelled the thing and it became level). استوى الرجل: the man's affairs became straight, his youth reached its end and he attained his full strength. استوى عليه: he prevailed over it and took control of it. استوى على ظهر الدابة: he settled on the back of the riding animal; one says استوى على سرير الملك (he sat on the throne of kingship) as a metonymy for taking possession of rule. استوى إلى الشيء: he directed himself to it. استوت به الأرض: he perished and was buried in it. استوى الطعام: the food was cooked." The root of the verb in the three-letter form is سوي يسوى; سوى الرجل: the man's affairs became straight.
He said in al-Asās: "The two things were equal (استوى الشيئان وتساويا), one of them equalled the other; so-and-so equals you in knowledge; he treated the two things equally (ساوى بين الشيئين وسوّى بينهما); I made this equal to that (ساويت هذا بهذا وسويته). al-Rāʿī said:
بجرد عليهنّ الأجلّة سوّيت ... بضيف الشتاء والبنين الأصاغر
(With short-haired horses wearing horse-cloths, treated equally with the winter guest and the little sons.)
i.e. he protects them as guests and children are protected. I straightened what was crooked and it became straight; may Allah the Exalted grant you a sound (سويّ) child with no disease or defect; they are on an equal footing (على سوية) in the matter, and equal (سواء); there is fairness (النصفة والسوية) in it; they are equal (سواء); they are all alike (سواسية) in evil; you two are equal (سيان); he is not your equal (بسيّ لك); the people did such-and-such, ولا سيما Zayd (especially Zayd). مكان سوى: a place midway between two limits. They came سوى فلان and سواءه (other than so-and-so). «فرآه في سواء الجحيم»: in its middle. He struck the middle of it (سواءه), and he struck him on the line (مستوى) of the parting of his hair. One of the Banū Aznam said:
نحن من خير معدّ نسبا ... ولنا قدما على الناس المهل
إذ ضربنا الصّمة الخير على ... مستوى مفرقه حتى انجدل
(We are of the best of Maʿadd in lineage, and ours of old is precedence over people, since we struck al-Ṣimma the good on the line of his parting until he fell to the ground.)
A man سواء القدم: one whose foot is flat, without a hollow in its sole. And among the figurative uses:
When I have prayed the dawn prayer I will head straight to you (استويت إليك): I will make for you directly, turning aside for nothing. «ثم استوى إلى السماء». He settled on the riding animal, the bed and the couch; his youth ended and he reached maturity (استوى); and he took control of (استوى على) the land." What is meant by it in the verse will come in the section on Rhetoric [Translator's note: so in the source; the discussion actually appears in the section on Benefits, as stated in the I'rab below].
(الثَّرى): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "الثرى, on the measure of الحصى, is the moisture of the earth; أثرت الأرض, with alif: its moisture increased. الثرى is also moist soil; if it is not moist, it is تراب (dust), and in that case it is not called ثرى." Also in it: "نديت الأرض ندى, of the تعب pattern: the land became moist, so it is ندية, like تعبة; it is made transitive with the hamza and with doubling; moisture (نداوة and ندوّة, with ḍamma and doubling) reached it." In al-Asās, al-Lisān and others: "A month of ثرى, a month of ترى, and a month of مرعى: i.e. the land is first moist, then you see (ترى) the green, then the plants grow tall until they are fit for grazing. The rain moistened (ثرى) the soil, يثريه, so it is مثري; the soil became moist (ثري), so it is ثرّ; I moistened (ثرّيت) the soil; and I moistened the sawīq (gruel)."
(وَأَخْفى): the discussion of it will come in the section on I'rab.

* I'rab:
(طه): the discussion of the opening letters of the surahs and their parsing has preceded.
(ما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى): ما is negating; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عليك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا; القرآن is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). لتشقى: the lām is for cause (taʿlīl), and تشقى is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. What is meant by الشقاء will come in the section on Benefits.
(إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى): إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); تذكرة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it cannot be an object of purpose of the stated أنزلنا, because that has already taken an object of purpose, namely لتشقى, so it cannot take another of the same kind; nor can لتشقى govern it, because the meaning would be corrupted. It was also said that تذكرة is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). al-Zamakhsharī chose that تذكرة be an object of purpose; he said: "Each of لتشقى and تذكرة is a reason for the verb, except that the first had to come with the lām because it does not belong to the agent of the verb being explained, so it lacked the condition for being accusative as an object; while with the second it was permissible to drop the lām and put it in the accusative, because the conditions are all met." Most of the grammarians and commentators follow this. al-Karkhī said in his comment on the words of al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī: "He indicated that the exception is disconnected and that تذكرة is an object of purpose, the governing word being the implied أنزلناه, not the stated one. Each of لتشقى and تذكرة is a reason for His saying ما أنزلنا; in لتشقى it was made transitive with the lām because the governing word differs, since the pronoun of أنزلنا is for Allah and the pronoun of لتشقى is for the Prophet, so the agent is not the same; while in تذكرة it is the same, because the one who reminds is Allah the Exalted, and He is the one who sends down, so it was put in the accusative without lām." Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī rejected its being an object of purpose or a badal (substitute) of لتشقى; he said: it is rather accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "We sent it down so that you may remind with it a reminding". We have cited these views, despite their divergence and mutual contradiction, only because we were unable to decide between them.
(تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّماواتِ الْعُلى): a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being نزلناه تنزيلا ("We sent it down a sending down"); [the verb] was omitted obligatorily, according to Ibn Mālik's saying:
والحذف حتم مع آت بدلا ... من فعله كندلا اللذ كاندلا
(Omission is obligatory with [a maṣdar] that comes as a substitute for its verb, like ندلا, which is like اندل.)
al-Zamakhsharī allowed several aspects in it, all of them sound; he said: "In the accusative of تنزيلا there are several aspects: that it be a badal of تذكرة if that is taken as a ḥāl, not if it is an object of purpose, because a thing is not given itself as its reason; that it be made accusative by an implied نزّل; that it be made accusative by أنزلنا, because the meaning of 'We sent it down only as a reminder' is 'We sent it down as a reminder'; that it be accusative by way of praise and specification (al-madḥ wa-l-ikhtiṣāṣ); and that it be made accusative by يخشى as its direct object, i.e. Allah sent it down as a reminder for whoever fears the revelation of Allah — which is a fine meaning and a clear parsing." ممن is attached to تنزيلا; the clause خلق الأرض والسموات is the ṣila (relative clause); and العلى is an adjective.
(الرَّحْمنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوى):
الرحمن is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو, or it is a mubtadaʾ. على العرش is attached to استوى; the clause استوى is a second khabar of the implied هو, or the khabar of الرحمن. The meaning of the istiwāʾ upon the Throne will come in the section on Benefits.
(لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما وَما تَحْتَ الثَّرى): له is a fronted khabar and ما a postponed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is the ṣila; وما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات, and وما بينهما likewise; ما is conjoined to ما, and تحت الثرى is an adverb attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of ما.
(وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفى): the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), brought to explain what Allah the Exalted has prescribed regarding supplication to Him. إن is conditional; تجهر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; بالقول, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to تجهر. فإنه: the fāʾ is a link because the apodosis is a nominal clause; إن and its noun, and the clause يعلم السر is its khabar. أخفى is conjoined to السر, i.e. "more hidden than it", so it is a comparative noun from خفي in the sense of being concealed and absent. Some allowed it to be a past verb, i.e. "and Allah has hidden His Unseen from His servants"; in our view that is not permissible, because in terms of wording it entails conjoining a verbal clause to a nominal one, if what it is conjoined to is the major clause, or conjoining a past verb to an imperfect one, if what it is conjoined to is the minor clause — and both are less than the best. In terms of meaning, it is clear that the intent is to urge abandoning loudness by removing its benefit, in that Allah knows the secret and what is more hidden than it — so what benefit remains in loudness? On this interpretation both [السر and أخفى] fit the abandoning of loudness; whereas if it is taken as a verb it departs from the intent of the context. Know that they sometimes omit من from أفعل when it is intended for comparison and the meaning of the verb while they still mean it, so it is as though uttered, as in زيد أكرم وأفضل ("Zayd is more generous and more excellent"); so it does not take alif and lām, just as it does not take them with من, because what exists by rule is like what exists in wording, i.e. "He knows the secret and what is more hidden than it". What shows that من is intended is that أخفى is a diptote, just as آخر is a diptote in your saying مررت برجل آخر, when you intend من with it even though you do not mention it. It is made indefinite only for intensity in hiddenness.
(اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى): الله is a mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause لا إله إلا هو is its khabar — the parsing of لا إله إلا هو has preceded in detail. له is a fronted khabar, الأسماء a postponed mubtadaʾ, and الحسنى an adjective of الأسماء; the clause is a second khabar. It is known that a broken plural of non-rational beings is treated as a singular feminine.

* Benefits:
1- History relates that Abū Jahl and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith said to him [ﷺ]:
"You are wretched (شقي) because you have abandoned the religion of your forefathers." So the intent was to refute that: the religion of Islam and this Quran are the ladder to attaining every success and the means of reaching every happiness, while what the unbelievers are in is wretchedness itself. It is also narrated that he, upon him be blessings and peace, prayed at night until his feet became swollen (اسمغدّت), i.e. swelled, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, and Jibrīl, upon him be peace, said to him: "Spare yourself, for it has a right over you." It may also be meant: do not exhaust yourself through excessive grief over the unbelief of Quraysh, since your only duty is conveying [the message], and it has not been prescribed for you that they believe, once you have not fallen short in delivering the message and offering good admonition. الشقاء comes in the sense of fatigue. Ibn Kaysān said: "The origin of الشقاء in the language is toil and fatigue"; and from it is the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
ذو العقل يشقى في النعيم بعقله ... وأخو الجهالة في الشقاوة ينعم
(The man of intellect is wretched amid bliss because of his intellect, while the brother of ignorance enjoys bliss amid wretchedness.)
2- The disconnected exception:
Excepting a thing from what is not of its kind has no meaning and no basis; so إلا in it is not for exception in the original sense, but rather in the sense of لكن ("but"), and this is what they call [Translator's note: the source has يسونه, a misprint for يسمونه] "the disconnected exception" (al-istithnāʾ al-munqaṭiʿ). Nevertheless, there must be a connection between what is excepted from and the excepted. An example is the saying of the Exalted «ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى», i.e. "but We sent it down as a reminder". So تذكرة is excepted from the interpreted maṣdar formed from تشقى with the implied أن after the lām of cause, because the meaning is "We did not send down the Quran for your wretchedness".

dervis-irab:71-76.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَ آمَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ): The clause آمنتم is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the speaker is Pharaoh. آمنتم: the hamza is for interrogation, rebuke and reproach; the first hamza has been dropped and the second lightened. It is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنتم; قبل is an adverb also attached to آمنتم; أن آذن لكم: the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi to قبل.
(إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ): إنّ and its ism; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and كبيركم is its khabar (predicate); الذي is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause علمكم السحر is the ṣila (relative clause); السحر is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of علمكم. I.e. Moses is your chief, meaning your teacher and your master and the highest of you in rank in the craft of magic. Al-Kisāʾī said: in the Hijaz, when a boy comes from his teacher, he says: «I have come from my kabīr». Al-Wāḥidī said: al-kabīr in the language is the chief, and for this reason the teacher is called al-kabīr. By this Pharaoh wanted to cast doubt upon the people and put it into their breasts, so that they would become suspicious and not believe; otherwise he knew that they had not learned from Moses, that he was not their chief, and that there was no connection between him and them.
(فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلافٍ): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; the lām is the lām that paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); أقطعن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I"; أيديكم is the mafʿūl bihi and أرجلكم is conjoined to أيديكم; من خلاف is a ḥāl (circumstantial) meaning "alternate"; من is for beginning, as if the cutting began from the opposition of one limb to the other.
(وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ): The wāw is a conjunction and لأصلبنكم is conjoined to لأقطعن; في is for containment (ẓarfiyya): the firm fixing of the crucified one to the trunk is likened to the firm placing of the thing contained in its container. It is attached to أصلبنكم. Further discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً وَأَبْقى): ولتعلمن is conjoined to لأصلبنكم; أينا is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أشد is the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تعلمن, because the verb has been suspended (ʿulliqa) by the interrogative أيّ. It is also permissible for أيّ to be a relative noun, made indeclinable because it is in annexation and the beginning of its ṣila has been omitted — its parallels have frequently been given — in which case it is the mafʿūl bihi of تعلمن, and أشد is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "he", and the clause أشد is the ṣila of the relative noun. أبقى is conjoined to أشد.
(قالُوا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلى ما جاءَنا مِنَ الْبَيِّناتِ وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنا): لن is a particle of negation, of the accusative and of the future; نؤثرك is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by لن; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; the clause is the object of their saying. على ما is attached to نؤثرك; the clause جاءنا is the ṣila; من البينات is attached to an omitted ḥāl; الذي is conjoined to ما. They put the mention of the Creator later by way of putting the lower before the higher; the discussion of putting forward and putting back will come in the section on Rhetoric [Translator's note: no such discussion appears in this entry's Rhetoric section]. It is also said that the wāw is for the oath and الذي is genitive by the wāw of the oath, i.e. sworn by, namely Allah the Exalted; فطرنا is the ṣila; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; the response to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "we shall not prefer you over the truth which has come to us".
(فَاقْضِ ما أَنْتَ قاضٍ إِنَّما تَقْضِي هذِهِ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; اقض is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; ما is the mafʿūl bihi; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and قاض is the khabar, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ which was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns; the clause أنت قاض is the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "decreeing it". إنما: [إنّ] restrained and [ما] the restraining particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), on the most likely view; تقضي is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; the object of تقضي is omitted, its implied form being "your need" or "your aim"; هذه is an adverb, الحياة is a badal (substitute) and الدنيا is a naʿt; the adverb is attached to تقضي. It is also permissible for ما to be a relative noun or maṣdariyya, being the ism of إنّ, with the khabar being the adverb. It is also permissible to parse هذه الحياة الدنيا as a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).
(إِنَّا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنا خَطايانا وَما أَكْرَهْتَنا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى): إنّ and its ism; the clause آمنا is its khabar; بربنا is attached to آمنا; the lām is for giving the reason and يغفر is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; لنا is attached to يغفر; ما is conjoined to خطايانا, i.e. "that He may forgive us our sins and forgive us also that which you compelled us to". You may also make the wāw inceptive and ما a mubtadaʾ, with the clause أكرهتنا as the ṣila and the khabar omitted, i.e. "is lifted from us and taken off our shoulders". عليه is attached to أكرهتنا; من السحر is a ḥāl; الله is a mubtadaʾ, خير is the khabar, and أبقى is conjoined to خير.
(إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِماً فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها وَلا يَحْيى): إنّ and its ism; من is a conditional noun that puts into the jussive, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; يأت is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil of يأت is latent, its implied form being "he"; ربه is the mafʿūl bihi and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; مجرما is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يأت. فإن: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; له is its fronted khabar and جهنم is its postponed ism; the clause لا يموت فيها is circumstantial, from the hāʾ in له or from جهنم; فيها is attached to يموت, and لا يحيا is conjoined to يموت.
(وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِناً قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحاتِ فَأُولئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجاتُ الْعُلى): ومن يأته مؤمنا: the parsing of its parallel has been given; the clause قد عمل الصالحات is a naʿt of مؤمنا. فأولئك: the fāʾ is linking and أولئك is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ; لهم is a fronted khabar and الدرجات is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك; the clause فأولئك is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من; العلى is a naʿt of الدرجات.
(جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى): جنات عدن is a badal from الدرجات العلى, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is a naʿt of جنات; خالدين فيها is a ḥāl of «من», and فيها is attached to خالدين; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, جزاء is the khabar, من is muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause تزكى is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of «لأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل»:
In His saying «وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ» there is in the speech an istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya (implicit, dependent metaphor). Its explanation is that He likened the crucified one's being upon the trunk to the containment of the buried one in his grave; then He used for the thing likened «في», which was coined for the thing it is likened to, I mean containment. So the metaphor ran in "being upon" and "containment", and dependently on that in على and في. Thus في is in its proper sense of containment, and this is the soundest of the opinions about it. It is also said that في means على, in which case there is no metaphor in the speech.

dervis-irab:9-16.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آنَسْتُ): I saw. الإيناس is clear seeing in which there is no doubt; from it comes إنسان العين (the pupil of the eye), because one sees things with it. Jarīr said:
إن العيون التي في طرفها حور ... قتلننا ثم لم يحيين قتلانا
يصرعن ذا اللب حتى لا حراك به ... وهن أضعف خلق الله إنسانا
(The eyes in whose glance there is a deep black-and-white have slain us, and then not revived our slain; they fell the man of sense until he cannot move, though they are the weakest of Allah's creation in their إنسان [i.e. pupil / as human beings].)
In his word إنسانا there is a marvellous tawriya (double entendre).
(بِقَبَسٍ): القبس is a firebrand of fire.
(طُوىً): a proper name for the valley. It is read without tanwīn as a definite feminine, a proper name for the spot. It was also said that it is altered (maʿdūl), even though the wording from which it was altered is not known, as though its origin were طاوي; so in that respect it is like جُمَع and كُتَع. He said in al-Qāmūs: "طوى, with ḍamma and kasra, and with tanwīn: a valley in Syria." The grammarians said: as for طوى, whoever makes it a diptote considers in it the feminine with reference to the spot, not alteration from طاو, because something other than alteration is possible, namely the feminine, so there is no reason to resort to alteration.
(أُخْفِيها): the discussion of it will come in the I'rab.
(فَتَرْدى): in al-Mukhtār: ردى, of the صدى pattern, i.e. he perished; and أرداه غيره (another destroyed him). ردى في البئر, تردى, يردي: when one falls into a well, or tumbles from a mountain.

* I'rab:
(وَهَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسى): the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāf), and the clause is resumptive, brought to relate the story of Moses so that the Prophet ﷺ might take him as an example in bearing the burdens of prophethood and the duties of the message, and in patience in enduring hardships and suffering terrors. أتاك is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حديث موسى is the fāʿil (agent). The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), its meaning being "Has not the story of Moses come to you?"; it was also said that its meaning is "The story of Moses has come to you".
(إِذْ رَأى ناراً فَقالَ لِأَهْلِهِ: امْكُثُوا إِنِّي آنَسْتُ ناراً): the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) الحديث, because it is an event, or to something implied, its implied form being اذكر ("remember"). The clause رأى is what the adverb is annexed to; نارا is a direct object; قال is conjoined to رأى; لأهله is attached to قال; the clause امكثوا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause إني gives the reason for the command to stay; إن and its noun, and the clause آنست is its khabar (predicate); and نارا is a direct object.
(لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدىً): لعل and its noun, and the clause آتيكم is its khabar; منها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of قبس. أو is a conjunction; أجد is conjoined to آتيكم; the agent of أجد is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "I"; على النار, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to أجد, and it keeps its proper sense of elevation (istiʿlāʾ), in accordance with the saying of al-Aʿshā:
لعمري لقد لاحت عيون كثيرة ... إلى ضوء نار في يفاع تحرق
تشب لمقرورين يصطليانها ... وبات على النار الندى والمحلق
(By my life, many eyes have looked towards the light of a fire burning on a hilltop, kindled for two chilled men warming themselves at it; and Generosity and al-Muḥallaq spent the night by the fire.)
i.e. the people of the fire are above the place close to it, as Sībawayh said about مررت بزيد: that it is contact with a place close to Zayd. هدى is a direct object, i.e. someone who will guide me on the way and show me to it. al-Farrāʾ said: He meant هاديا ("a guide"), but mentioned it in the form of the maṣdar (verbal noun); or He expressed it with the maṣdar for the purpose of intensity, with omission of a muḍāf, i.e. ذا هدى ("someone possessing guidance").
(فَلَمَّا أَتاها نُودِيَ يا مُوسى): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, the implied form being "so he headed towards the fire". لما is temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) or a linking particle; أتاها is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause نودي has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and يا موسى is the vocative particle and the one addressed.
(إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوىً): إن and its noun; أنا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun, or a mubtadaʾ (subject); ربك is the khabar of إني, or the khabar of أنا, the clause being the khabar of إن — the first is preferable. فاخلع: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition); اخلع is an imperative verb with a latent agent; نعليك is a direct object; the clause إنك gives the reason for the removing; إن and its noun, and بالوادي is its khabar; المقدس is an adjective; and طوى is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Its being a diptote or not has already been discussed in the section on Vocabulary.
(وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِما يُوحى): the wāw is a conjunction; أنا is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause اخترتك, of verb, agent and object, is the khabar. فاستمع: the fāʾ is a conjunction; استمع is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; لما is attached to استمع; the clause يوحى is the ṣila (relative clause); and يوحى is passive.
(إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي): the clause is a badal of ما in لما يوحى. إن and its noun; أنا is an emphasis of the pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; الله is the khabar of إنني or the khabar of أنا, the clause being the khabar of إن; and the clause لا إله إلا أنا is a second khabar. فاعبدني: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; اعبدني is an imperative verb with a latent agent, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the object. أقم الصلاة is conjoined to اعبدني; لذكري is attached to أقم; it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. "so that you remember Me in it". It was also said that the maṣdar is annexed to its agent, i.e. "for My remembering you".
(إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكادُ أُخْفِيها لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى): إن, its noun and its khabar. أكاد is a defective imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation; its noun is latent, its implied form being "I"; the clause أخفيها is the khabar, i.e. "I wish to hide its time", or "I am close to hiding it, so that I do not say it is coming". It may also be meant "I almost reveal it", for the verb أخفى is one of the aḍdād (words with opposite meanings); further discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric. لتجزى: the lām is for cause (taʿlīl), and تجزى is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن; it is attached to أخفيها, or to آتية, with the clause أكاد أخفيها being parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) between them. كل نفس is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); بما is attached to تجزى; and the clause تسعى is the ṣila. It is also possible that ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. "with the recompense of its striving", with omission of a muḍāf.
(فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْها مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِها وَاتَّبَعَ هَواهُ فَتَرْدى): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; لا is prohibitive; يصدنك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive by prohibitive لا; the kāf is a direct object; عنها is attached to يصدنك; من is the agent; the clause لا يؤمن is the ṣila; بها is attached to يؤمن; اتبع هواه is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. فتردى: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and تردى is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, with an implied fatḥa on the alif.

* Rhetoric:
The device of al-ibhām (deliberate vagueness):
In the saying of the Exalted «لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدىً». It is an exalted device containing many sublime and subtle meanings. It is the opposite of conciseness (ījāz) and the opposite of prolixity (iṭnāb). Its definition is that the speaker comes to a single meaning which he could indicate with few words, and indicates it with many words — not to make the dull understand or the distant hear, nor for affirmation and emphasis, but to bring a meaning that branches out into several matters, each of which is independent in its sense. He said «لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس» and did not state the matter decisively, so as not to promise what he was not certain of fulfilling — and what a beautiful piece of wisdom this is, a lesson for those who dole out promises carelessly and give no thought to fulfilling them. Then he said «لعلي أجد على النار هدى», and this contains another meaning that then branches out: guidance is the principal meaning; then the guidance may be through the fire itself, by the illumination latent in it in particular, or through the people who kindle it. From this it is understood implicitly that he had lost his way together with his family who were accompanying him — namely his wife, the daughter of Shuʿayb, who had given birth to a son on the road on a wintry, dark, cold night, said also to have been snowy. When he was at a loss, he perceived the fire and said what he said. Then by guidance its other, figurative meaning may be intended, i.e. "perhaps I will be guided by the light of knowledge", because the thoughts of the righteous are immersed in aspirations [Translator's note: the source has الهمم; possibly الهموم, "cares"]. So blessed is the Speaker of these words.
In the saying of the Exalted «إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكادُ أُخْفِيها لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى» there is ibhām — a wondrous device in which the speaker says words that bear two different meanings, neither of which is distinguished from the other. The word أخفيها, first of all, means several things, among them:
a- I.e. "I almost hide it, so that I do not say it is coming", through the excess of My will to hide it; and were it not for the kindness that lies in announcing its coming while obscuring its time, I would not have announced it.
b- "I almost hide it from Myself."
Further, in some dialects أخفاه has come in the sense of خفاه, so it is one of the aḍdād, i.e. "I almost reveal it", because its time is near; and with this the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays has been explained:
فإن تدفنوا الداء لا نخفه ... وإن تبعثوا الحرب لا نقعد
(If you bury the malady, we will not uncover it; and if you rouse war, we will not sit still.)
i.e. if you conceal the rancour that is between us, we too will conceal it and not reveal it.
However, the best interpretation of the noble verse is that what is meant is "I almost remove its covering", i.e. reveal it, since الخفاء is the covering, and it is also what a woman puts over her clothes [Translator's note: the source has نيابها, read as ثيابها] to cover herself. Then the Arabs say أخفيته when you remove its covering, just as you say أشكيته and أعتبته when you remove his complaint and his reproach.
Abū ʿAlī al-Qālī said: "al-Liḥyānī said: خفيت الشيء أخفيه خفيا وخُفيا, when I brought it out and revealed it; and he recited for Imruʾ al-Qays:
خفاهنّ من أنفاقهنّ كأنما ... خفاهن ودق من سحاب مركب
(It drove them out of their burrows, as if what drove them out were the downpour of a piled-up cloud.) [Translator's note: the source has ورق; the familiar wording of the verse is ودق.]
Abū ʿAlī said: others transmit it 'من عشيّ مجلّب', i.e. resounding [Translator's note: the source has عشني]. One says اختفيت الشيء, i.e. I revealed it; the people of the Ḥijāz call the grave-robber المختفي, because he brings out the shrouds of the dead. أخفيت الشيء أخفيه إخفاء, when I covered it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said «أَكادُ أُخْفِيها» — and this is the reading of the generality — i.e. I reveal it. Abū ʿUbayda said: أخفيت الشيء: I concealed it and I revealed it. One says: I called on Allah خفية and خِفية, i.e. in a low voice."
A collection of aḍdād (words with opposite meanings) in the language:
Among the aḍdād is الجلل, for the great and the insignificant. Of the first is the poet's saying:
ولئن عفوت لا عفون جللا ... ولئن سطوت لأوهننّ عظمي
(If I pardon, I shall pardon something great; and if I strike, I shall weaken my own bone.)
And of the second is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays when his father was killed:
بقتل بني أسد ربهم ... ألا كل شيء سواه جلل
(For the Banū Asad's killing of their lord — indeed everything besides it is trivial.)
Among them: غابر, for what has passed and what is to come; الجون, for white and black; البين, for distance and nearness; الصريم: night and day; الناصع, white and black; الأمم, for the great and the slight; الناهل, for the one whose thirst is quenched and the thirsty; وراء, in the sense of "in front" and "behind"; بعت الشيء, when you sell it to another, and بعته, you bought it; شعبت الشيء:
I mended it and I split it; الصارخ, for the one who calls for help and the one who helps; الهاجد, for one who prays at night and one who sleeps; الوهدة: rise and descent; التعزير, for honouring and humiliating; التقريظ, for praise and blame; ترب, for the rich and the poor; الإهماد, for speed in travelling and for staying; عسعس: when it approached and when it departed; and القرء, for menstruation and purity.

dervis-irab:77-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَبَساً): with two fatḥas. He said in al-Qāmūs: «يبس الشيء ييبس, of the patterns ʿalima and ḥasiba, yabsan and yubsan, and اتّبس: it was moist and then dried, so it is يبس, يبس, يابس, يبوس, يبيس and أيبس». Some Arabs were heard to say: «جمّرت الخبز كي يابس ظهره»: I put embers on the bread so that its top would dry; «وقد يبست»: when its moisture had gone. «عود يابس» (a dry stick), «عيدان يبس» (dry sticks); «السفينة لا تجري على يبس» (the ship does not run on dry land): «طريقا في البحر يبسا»; «هي ترعى اليبس» (it grazes on the dry plants); al-yabīs is whatever plants have dried, so the common people's use of al-nabāt al-yabīs (dried vegetables) to be cooked out of their season is beyond reproach. Among the figurative uses: «قد يبس ما بينهما» when the two have cut off relations, and «لا توبس الثرى بيني وبينك» (do not dry up the moist earth between me and you). Jarīr said:
أتغلب أولي حلفة ما ذكرتكم ... بسوء ولكني عتبت على بكر
(O Taghlib, I swear an oath that I have not mentioned you with evil; rather I reproached Bakr.)
فلا توبسوا بيني وبينكم الثرى ... فإن الذي بيني وبينكم مثري
(So do not dry up the moist earth between me and you, for what is between me and you is still moist.)
(دَرَكاً): with two fatḥas, i.e. that Pharaoh and his troops overtake you. Al-darak and al-dark, with two fatḥas and with fatḥa on the dāl and sukūn on the rāʾ, is catching up, attaining a need, and the furthest bottom of a thing; one says: «بلغ الغواص درك البحر» (the diver reached the bottom of the sea), and one says «فرس درك الطريدة», i.e. a horse that overtakes the quarry. From it is their saying: «ما لحقك من درك فعليّ خلاصه» (whatever liability overtakes you, its settlement is upon me). So the usage rijāl al-darak (gendarmes) is correct and beyond reproach.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبادِي): The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; the lām is the response to the omitted oath; أوحينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); إلى موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوحينا; أن is explicative (mufassira); أسر, with a disjunctive hamza, from أسرى, is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; بعبادي is attached to أسر, i.e. "travel with them by night".
(فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقاً فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَساً لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً وَلا تَخْشى): فاضرب is conjoined to أسر, i.e. "make", from their saying «ضرب له في ماله سهما» (he assigned him a share in his wealth) and «ضرب اللبن» (he made the mud bricks); so the common people's saying «ضرب لبنا» is beyond reproach. لهم is attached to اضرب, i.e. standing in place of the second object; طريقا is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في البحر is a naʿt (adjective) and يبسا is a second naʿt. It is a description of what it would become, as will come in the section on Rhetoric; or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description for intensification, like «رجل عدل» and «صدق». The clause لا تخاف is circumstantial, from the fāʿil of اضرب, i.e. "strike, not fearing"; or a naʿt of طريقا with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "you will not fear in it"; or it is a resumptive clause; the first is more evident. لا is negative and تخاف is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil being "you"; دركا is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ولا تخشى is conjoined to لا تخاف.
(فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ): The fāʾ is a conjunction; أتبعهم is a past verb taking two objects, the second of which has been omitted, the implied form being "so Pharaoh made his punishment follow them", and the hāʾ is the first object. It is also said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on the second object, the implied form being "so Pharaoh made his troops follow them"; it is then like the saying of the Exalted: «وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ». أتبع has come as transitive to two objects, both stated explicitly; He said «وَأَتْبَعْناهُمْ ذرياتهم» [Translator's note: the quotation as printed does not match the Quranic text; cf. al-Ṭūr 52:21 «وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ» and al-Qaṣaṣ 28:42 «وَأَتْبَعْناهُمْ فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا لَعْنَةً»]. It is also said that it means تبع, transitive to one object, in which case بجنوده is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فغشيهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; غشيهم is a past verb and the hāʾ is its object, i.e. it overwhelmed them; ما is the fāʿil, and the clause غشيهم [Translator's note: printed «عشيهم»] is the ṣila (relative clause). It is a case of ibhām (vagueness), and it will be discussed a second time in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَما هَدى): The wāw is a conjunction, with a putting forward and putting back in the speech, because his leading his people astray was naturally before the drowning [Translator's note: printed «العرق», evidently for «الغرق»]. أضل is a past verb, فرعون is the fāʿil and قومه is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause وما هدى is conjoined to أضل. The discussion of this conjunction and the sarcasm in it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْناكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ): يا is a vocative particle and بني إسرائيل is a vocative (munādā) in annexation; قد is a particle of affirmation; أنجيناكم is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; من عدوكم is attached to أنجيناكم.
(وَواعَدْناكُمْ جانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوى): وواعدناكم is conjoined to أنجيناكم; واعدناكم is a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; جانب الطور is the second mafʿūl bihi on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the coming to the side"; it cannot be an adverb because it is delimited. الأيمن is a naʿt of جانب. نزلنا is conjoined to what precedes it, completing the enumeration of the worldly and religious blessings that came upon them one after another; عليكم is attached to نزلنا; المن is the mafʿūl bihi and السلوى is conjoined to المن; mention of both has already been given. The address is either to the Children of Israel after their rescue from the sea and the destruction of Pharaoh and his troops, or it is directed to the Jews in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, who were addressed with the blessings Allah had bestowed on their forefathers; and despite that they were ungrateful for the blessing, belittled it and denied it. So they are the cause of causes in the various circumstances of time and place, and they are the instrument for obstructing peace at every moment.
(كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّباتِ ما رَزَقْناكُمْ وَلا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي): كلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; من طيبات is attached to كلوا; ما is the mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: ما is in fact genitive as muḍāf ilayhi of طيبات; the source says mafʿūl bihi]; the clause رزقناكم is the ṣila. ولا تطغوا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تطغوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; فيه is attached to تطغوا. فيحل: the fāʾ is of causation (sababiyya); يحل is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن because it occurs in the response to a prohibition; عليكم is attached to يحل, and غضبي is the fāʿil. It is also said that it is conjoined, in which case it too is a prohibition.
(وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوى): The wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يحلل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عليه is attached to يحلل; غضبي is the fāʿil of يحلل; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قد is a particle of affirmation and هوى is a past verb, i.e. he perished; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من, on the precise view.
(وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً ثُمَّ اهْتَدى): The wāw is a conjunction; إنّ and its ism; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and غفار is the khabar of إنّ; لمن is attached to غفار; the clause تاب is the ṣila; آمن and عمل are conjoined; صالحا is the mafʿūl bihi, or a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "he did a righteous deed". ثم اهتدى is a conjunction placed later in view of the end point, because of its distance from the beginning of guidance, or because of the disparity between the two ranks; for persisting in repentance, faith and righteous deeds is the basic condition for the acceptance of deeds.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are various kinds of devices, which we set out below:

1- Al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical trope):
This is in His saying يبسا, because it was not dry when Allah the Exalted addressed him, but [it is so called] in view of what it would become, like the saying of the Exalted «إِنِّي أَرانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً». Discussion of it has already been given in detail.

2- Al-ibhām (vagueness):
This is in His saying «فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ», i.e. there came over them and overwhelmed them, of the terrible matter which was beyond their capacity to bear, that whose essence cannot be grasped nor its depth fathomed. It is one of the comprehensive expressions (jawāmiʿ al-kalim) whose wording is little and whose meaning branches out widely.

3- Al-tahakkum (sarcasm):
Discussion of it has been given several times; here it is in His saying «وَما هَدى». It is well known that sarcasm is that the speaker brings an expression while what is meant is the opposite of its meaning, as in his saying «إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد», where their purpose was to describe him with the opposite of these two qualities. As for the saying of the Exalted «وَما هَدى», its content is what actually happened, so it is then merely a report that he did not guide his people; so where is the sarcasm? But the usage in something like «ما هدى زيد عمرا» (Zayd did not guide ʿAmr) is that guidance is established for Zayd in himself, but he is blamed for not having guided ʿAmr. Pharaoh, however, is astray in himself; indeed, misguidance is ingrained in his nature, latent in him as innate natures are latent. So how could it be imagined that he would guide anyone else? Hence he combined the two faults, and evil surrounded him from two sides; so it is fitting that one like him, having become a laughing-stock, be mocked and become an object of sarcasm.

4- Al-majāz al-ʿaqlī (rational trope):
And in the saying of the Exalted «وَواعَدْناكُمْ جانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ»: someone may say that the appointment was made with Moses, upon him be peace, so how has it been attributed to them? The clarification of the precise answer — which I have not seen anyone give its full due — is that it is a majāz ʿaqlī: the appointment from Allah was attributed to them, just as things perceived are attributed to what has no perception, by way of majāz ʿaqlī. This is among the loftiest that a tactful style reaches. You say to the son of your friend who is a wrongdoer floundering in the mire of disgrace: «I have known you [all] to be people of intelligence and self-restraint», meaning to attribute to him what is as far from him as things perceived are far from non-rational beings when they are attributed to them by way of majāz ʿaqlī.

dervis-irab:124-135.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضَنْكاً): with tanwīn, a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "narrow, straitened"; for this reason it was not put in the feminine by saying ضنكة, according to the rule mentioned by the author of al-Khulāṣa (the Alfiyya):
ونعتوا بمصدر كثيرا ... فالتزموا الإفراد أو التذكيرا
(They often used a maṣdar as an adjective, and then kept it singular and masculine.)
In al-Qāmūs: "al-ḍank is narrowness in everything, for masculine and feminine alike. One says ḍanuka, on the pattern of karuma, ḍankan, ḍanāka and ḍunūka: it became narrow." It was also read ضنكى, on the pattern faʿlā.
(يَهْدِ لَهُمْ): i.e. "it becomes guided/clear for them"; so it is intransitive, and its meaning is "it becomes clear".
(آناءِ اللَّيْلِ): plural of إنى, with kasra on the hamza and a short final alif, like معى with kasra on the mīm.
In al-Mukhtār: "Ānāʾ al-layl are its hours. Al-Akhfash said its singular is إنى, like معى; it has also been said that its singular is أني and أنو. One says: two hours (أنوان and انيان) of the night have passed."
(مُتَرَبِّصٌ): one who waits for what the matter will come to.

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكاً): the wāw is a conjunction joining this to the preceding conditional sentence, namely «فمن اتبع هداي»; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive (majzūm), a mubtadaʾ (subject); أعرض is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; عن ذكري is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعرض. فإن: the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; له is its fronted khabar (predicate), معيشة is its postponed noun, and ضنكا is an adjective (naʿt). The nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من. (وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ أَعْمى) ونحشره: the wāw is resumptive; نحشر is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to نحشره; أعمى is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in نحشره. It was also read with the jussive, as a conjoining onto the position of «فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكاً».
(قالَ: رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيراً): رب is the one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf to the first-person yāʾ, which has been omitted. لم: the lām is a preposition, and the interrogative ما is in the position of genitive by the lām; the alif of the interrogative ما has been dropped, as is the rule; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حشرتني. حشرتني is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; أعمى is a ḥāl; the wāw is of the ḥāl; قد is a particle of verification; كنت is kāna and its noun, and بصيرا is the khabar of كنت.
(قالَ كَذلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آياتُنا فَنَسِيتَها وَكَذلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنْسى): كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a gathering like that", or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus". أتتك آياتي [Translator's note: the source writes آياتي here; the Quranic text is آياتُنا] is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil. فنسيتها: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and نسيتها is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. وكذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and اليوم is an adverb attached to تنسى.
